content.rationale:
The record verb has two selections of the same recording. In its path form, without --to (yrmxrywl), with no id at all (ouyrkmlr) or with no path (R1) it refuses and places nothing; an argument the form does not name refuses, named (R2), and its arguments are recognized in any order (R3); a named path that cannot be placed - no working-copy edit, or not owned by the target (R4) - refuses, named, placing nothing; when the --to id maps to neither a valid node nor the root it refuses before placing, naming the id (D21, tsspuwzo, xtmprysl) and touching nothing (qyynqqpx); when the named target maps to no node it refuses, naming the id, and places nothing (uzlvzrpv); otherwise it brackets the recording through M-markers-capture - the lifecycle table's recording case (S5-lifecycle) - reading the working copy's changed paths through M-jj-status (S3-status), attributing with M-node-own over the resolved document (the ownership rule, D2, xzxtxymq, S2-own) with D6's placement rule (roqpxulw) deciding which change owns which edit, and moving the named paths into the named change through M-jj-place (S3-place). Purpose is named, never inferred (D13, rvyrosmp); it creates no node (lypvkskv), lands no edit outside an owning change (xklsyrrv), and writes nothing on success (O7-record, wvqzoqvx). It resolves the id through M-node-resolve (hence M-node-load), names the file through M-store-path, reads through M-store-read across the runner (M-jj), builds its refusals through M-refusal, takes the injected context (M-context, M-context-injection), and returns its lines for the envelope to write (M-output-return) under M-route's handler shape - the table's Verb type, which its signature must match - carrying its own --help text (xlvoxmyl/rwlywqrk, per oqnsuzqu) - answered before the store is taken, so a root-less context still answers it (H1, qtqnuqxo), as do the form's refusals. I1-serde (orrvsxqq) fixes the JSON layer the module is written against - serde and serde_json, the crate's own `Value` and the derive. It takes the store through the context's fallible accessor for the capture bracket, after the surface is answered (S3-root-required). The read's refusal site (S2-read-refusal-site, vollyzvn) is this invocation's: a target whose document cannot be read refuses, naming it. A recording answers its target even when the placement refuses (S5-record-named, wotmvzyt): the window it kept may hold work that landed before the refusal, so the marker is what undo reverts. The capture call is the recording bracket (M-markers-capture, okkvnnvm): it snapshots the paths the recording names - the target's owned set in the path form, the landable set in the source form - and stores one journal entry, so record hands across the set it places, with the path the draft's document adds kept with a null before side and a present after side so undo removes it (vmwvnnzv).

The source form `--from <handle>` is that same recording reached through the one value that picks a draft out (uvrltuvo, vmwvnnzv): `record --from <handle> --to <node> [path...]` lands one open draft. The handle names the one document at `.deccy/work/<handle>.json`, read through M-draft-registry (rroqqrzq), whose read checks the record against the carried schema and refuses a non-conforming or misnamed document by the path it refused (ntypuupx); an absent handle is a record that is not there, and a document the read refuses is never surfaced as a record, so either way the invocation refuses and places nothing (uvrltuvo). `--to` stays required and must be the node the record names (uvrltuvo): a `--to` naming another node, or a record whose state is not `open`, refuses and changes nothing; a source whose edit reference is the change `--to` names - compared as the owning change id, never a commit id, a workspace path or the handle - refuses because the recording would be the change into itself (uvrltuvo, vkkwusty). The landable set is the union of the target change's current owned set and the ref paths the draft's node document adds (vmwvnnzv): M-node-own over the document resolved at the `--to` change gives the node document plus its array `content.ref` paths (D2, xzxtxymq), and the draft's own document - `nodes/<id>.json` in the draft's workspace - is read there and parsed, every string in its array `content.ref` joining the set, so a path the draft newly owns is landable even though the target does not own it yet; the document itself is already in the current owned set and lands like any changed path, and a ref the draft's document no longer lists stays in the set through the target's current set. The content the draft's workspace carries for each path of that set is compared with the content the owning change holds, read through M-store-read across M-jj, and only the paths whose content differs are moved (uvrltuvo, vmwvnnzv, qrqsxyzz): an added ref is a change because the target holds nothing at it, a dropped ref the draft deletes is a carried deletion and a change, a dropped ref the draft leaves alone is not a change, and a newly listed ref that neither side carries is not a change while the document that lists it still lands. The identity of each compared path is the one M-draft-identity renders (ttkuyvxp) over the bytes that same read returns, so the landing's comparison agrees with the base the opening wrote; a draft whose content for the whole set is unchanged has no changed path and no landing, so the invocation refuses and the record stays `open` (uvrltuvo). The `[path...]` arguments are optional only in this form, because the draft and the landable set name the edits; when given they state the changed landable set and never select a partial landing - every named path must be in the set and changed, every changed path of the set must be named, and a disagreement refuses with nothing placed (uvrltuvo, vmwvnnzv).

The landing is refused when any open record naming the node is stale (ptlmptoy, qrqsxyzz): every `.json` record in the registry is scanned through M-draft-registry (rroqqrzq), each one that is `open` and names the `--to` node is compared path by path against the owned set as it stands at the landing - its base's entries against the content identity of the owned content now, with equal values agreeing and a value that no longer matches, a base path the owned set has lost, or an owned path the base does not hold each a difference - and the refusal names every stale handle with that record's differing paths, not only the addressed record's (qrqsxyzz, ptlmptoy). The comparison reads the owned set at the change that owns the node, never the draft's workspace or the working copy's dirty set, so a draft's own unrecorded edits are not a difference (qrqsxyzz). The baseline is the target's current set and never the union the landing places, so a ref the draft's document adds is a placement to make and not a difference that makes any record stale (vmwvnnzv).

The placement and the state write are one recording (qvkuluyw): the draft's working copy is settled first so the squash source carries the content that was compared, then the changed owned paths move into the `--to` change through the same S3-place mechanism - `jj squash --into <id>` - with the draft's workspace named as the source; the landing is non-interactive, so when the draft's working copy and the node's change both carry a description it keeps the destination's and discards the source's rather than asking a person to combine the two (`--use-destination-message`), and the node's change is left with the description it had (rvyrosmp, zylowqkr, uvrltuvo). The record is written `landed` through M-draft-registry inside the same M-markers-capture bracket, so there is no marker of its own, no second operation, and the landed record is retained rather than deleted (qvkuluyw, vkkwusty); the bracket snapshots the landable set, so that one journal entry covers every path the landing can touch - including the ref the draft's document adds, whose before side is null - and undo removes what the document added and restores what it dropped (vmwvnnzv, okkvnnvm). The bracket is invoked from the recording's own workspace with the draft's working copy as the source, so the edits that move are the draft's rather than the invoking workspace's, and the workspace that makes the recording is the one jj updates as the target's change is rewritten. Every refusal precedes the bracket, so a refused landing places nothing and writes no record state (uvrltuvo); on success nothing is written to stdout (O7-record), no node or edge is created, no edit lands outside an owning change, and the other open records naming the node are left exactly as they were, still open and still carrying their own bases (uvrltuvo, vkkwusty).
